map.Lessons 5-4 & 5-5 — compound area and th: Lessons 5-4 & 5-5. Compound area. The volume of rectangular prisms, with fractional edges. Three gates come before the concrete sets.
map.Previously: the floor plans were drawn,: Last time: we drew the floor plans. Hargrove used one base for the trapezoid. We showed it to the whole council.
map.Previously, in Episode 1: the crew's dra: Last time, in Episode 1: the crew's plans beat Hargrove's. Now the cement truck comes Friday. The forms have to be RIGHT.
The boards for the patio go down today. Concrete waits for no one.
map.I'll just… independently verify your mea: I will just… check your sizes myself. With my own tape. Just so you know.
The patio is not a rectangle. It is an L. No one formula fits. So we SPLIT it into shapes. Each shape has a formula.
map.Compound figures get decomposed: cut the: Compound figures get decomposed. Cut them up. Use rectangles and triangles. Find each area. Then add them up.
map.The survey sketch, taped to a form board: The sketch is taped to a board. One L, five labels.
map.Big rectangle, 8 by 5. Little rectangle,: Big rectangle, 8 by 5. Small rectangle, 4 by 3. One cut line. Now it is two easy problems.
map.Decomposition protocol: area survives cu: Decompose rule: cutting does not change area. The L's total is the sum of its parts. No more, no less.
map.Reader — total the patio before Fenwick: Reader, add up the patio fast. Fenwick will "check" it wrong!
map.The L-shaped patio decomposes into a 8 m: The L-shaped patio decomposes into two rectangles. One is 8 m × 5 m. One is 4 m × 3 m. What is the TOTAL area to pour?
map.Conceptual: area survives cutting — find: Conceptual: cutting does not change area. Find each rectangle's area. Then add the two.
map.Procedural: big piece 8 × 5. Small piece: Procedural: big piece 8 × 5. Small piece 4 × 3. Then add the two products. Not the side lengths.
map.Soil order time. Volume is length × widt: Time to order soil. Volume is length × width × height. Three sides. Multiply them all.
map.Fractional edges are not optional decima: Fractional edges count too. 2.5 metres deep means each cubic metre counts. That includes the half-layers.
map.Volume of a rectangular prism = length ×: Volume of a rectangular prism = length × width × height. It works for a fraction or decimal edge too.
map.Two boxes, two pours, reader. Don't drop: Two boxes, two pours, reader. Do not drop the half metre.
map.Two pours. The big planter is 4 m × 3 m: Two pours. The big plant box is 4 m × 3 m × 2.5 m. The herb box is 2 m × 1.5 m × 1 m. Volume of each?
map.Conceptual: volume fills three direction: Conceptual: volume fills three ways. So multiply all three edges. A 2.5 means the half-layer of cubes counts too.
map.Procedural: big planter: 4 × 3 = 12, the: Procedural: big plant box: 4 × 3 = 12, then 12 × 2.5. Herb box: 2 × 1.5 = 3, then × 1.
map.Thursday. Fenwick posts his \"independen: Thursday. Fenwick puts his own "check" on the fence.
map.The plans say HALF a metre deep. He just: The plans say HALF a metre deep. He made one fake digit. That doubled the city's concrete bill.
map.One wrong dimension doesn't add a little: One wrong side does not add a small error. It MULTIPLIES the whole answer.
map.The stage deck: a 10-by-6 rectangle plus: The stage deck: a 10-by-6 rectangle plus a triangle wing. Two shapes in one. Episode 1 rules apply.
map.Friday's pour needs BOTH numbers: the de: Friday's pour needs BOTH numbers. The deck's area, in square metres. The slab's volume, in cubic metres. Then we check Fenwick.
map.Truck's here! Reader — run the final num: The truck is here! Reader, do the last numbers. I will hold the chute!
map.Boss Gate: the deck's compound area, the: Boss Gate: the deck's area. The slab's true volume. And the mistake in Fenwick's 24.
map.BOSS GATE. Three locks. The concrete is: BOSS GATE. Three locks. The concrete is setting now. No rush. (Okay, some rush.)
map.The truck is running. Three locks: the s: The truck is running. Three locks. The stage deck is a 10 m × 6 m rectangle plus a triangle (base 6 m, height 4 m). The slab below it is 6 m × 4 m × 0.5 m. Fenwick billed the slab at 24 m³.
map.Conceptual: the deck is compound — recta: Conceptual: the deck is two shapes. Add the rectangle area and the triangle area. The slab is a prism. Multiply its three edges. 0.5 is one of them.
map.Procedural: Lock 1: (10 × 6) + (6 × 4 ÷: Procedural: Lock 1: (10 × 6) + (6 × 4 ÷ 2). Lock 2: 6 × 4 × 0.5. Lock 3: compare Fenwick's 24 to your Lock 2. What did he change?
map.Twelve cubic metres ordered, twelve pour: Twelve cubic metres ordered. Twelve poured. None wasted. The city said no to Fenwick's bill.
map.Next week: paint and canvas. Everything: Next week: paint and cloth. All we built must get WRAPPED. Wrapping is surface area.
map.Compound area.Cut the shape into pieces: Compound area.Cut the shape into pieces with formulas. Then add: the L-patio = (8×5) + (4×3) = 52 m².
map.Volume.Length × width × height — and a 2: Volume.Length × width × height. A 2.5 m edge means the halves count: 4 × 3 × 2.5 = 30 m³.
map.Audit habit.One faked dimension multipli: Audit habit.One fake side multiplies the whole bill. Check each factor.
map.completed Unit 5 · Episode 2: Solid Grou: did Unit 5 · Episode 2: Solid Ground. You can find compound area. You can find the volume of rectangular prisms.
map.A different L: a 6 × 4 rectangle joined: A new L: two rectangles. One is 6 × 4. One is 3 × 2.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.An L is a 5 × 4 rectangle plus a 2 × 3 r: An L is two rectangles: 5 × 4 and 2 × 3. Find the total area.
map.Times the height: 6 × 1.5 = 9 cubic metr: Times the height: 6 × 1.5 = 9 cubic metres. The .5 adds a half-layer: 6 + 3 = 9.
map.A different deck: 8 × 5 rectangle plus a: A new deck: 8 × 5 rectangle plus a triangle base 4, height 3.
map.Its slab 5 × 4 × 0.5 = 10 m³ — half a me: Its slab 5 × 4 × 0.5 = 10 m³. Half a metre deep means HALF of 5 × 4.
map.40 + 12 = 52 m². Forms locked — Fenwick': 40 + 12 = 52 m². Forms locked. Fenwick's tape stays in his pocket.
map.That's only the BIG rectangle. The L has: That is only the BIG rectangle. The L has a second piece. Add it.
map.You added side lengths. Area multiplies: You added side lengths. Multiply first. Each rectangle is length × width. THEN add.
map.Cut along the dashed line: one 8×5 piece: Cut on the dashed line. One 8×5 piece. One 4×3 piece. Two products, one sum.
map.30 m³ and 3 m³ — soil ordered to the cub: 30 m³ and 3 m³. The soil order is just right. Even Noah's math tool bows to you.
map.You dropped the half metre! 2.5, not 2 —: You dropped the half metre! It is 2.5, not 2. The half-layer is real soil.
map.You ADDED the edges. Volume multiplies:: You ADDED the edges. Volume multiplies all three sides.
map.Multiply all three edges of each box. Es: Multiply all three edges of each box. Estimate first: 4×3 is 12. And 2.5 of those layers…
map.Lock 3 holds. Compare 24 to your Lock 2: Lock 3 holds. Compare 24 to your Lock 2 answer. It is just DOUBLE. Which side doubles it?
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. 72 m² of deck, 12 m³ of: ALL LOCKS OPEN. 72 m² of deck. 12 m³ of slab. We caught Fenwick's doubled depth before the bill cleared. SOLID GROUND.
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
